concept: Energy transfer between system and surroundings
prompt: When ammonium nitrate dissolves in water in a beaker, the beaker becomes cold. Identify the system and the surroundings, and state the direction of energy transfer.
markscheme:
System: the dissolving ammonium nitrate (the chemical change); surroundings: the water, beaker and air **(A1)**

Energy transfers from the surroundings into the system, so the surroundings cool; total energy is conserved **(A1)**
**C.** Melting needs energy to overcome attractions between particles. Combustion, neutralisation and condensation release energy.

concept: Relative stability of reactants and products
prompt: For an exothermic reaction, compare the stability of the reactants and products, and describe the energy profile.
markscheme: Products are lower in enthalpy, so more stable than the reactants **(R1)**; the profile rises to a transition state (activation energy) and falls to a product level below the reactant level, with $\Delta H<0$ **(A1)**

prompt: 50.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl is mixed with 50.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ NaOH. The temperature rises by 6.8 °C. Calculate the enthalpy change of neutralisation. (Assume the solution has density 1.00 g cm⁻³ and $c=4.18\ \text{J g}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.)
markscheme:
$q=mc\Delta T=100\times4.18\times6.8=2.84\times10^{3}$ J **(M1)(A1)**

$n(\text{H}_2\text{O})=0.0500$ mol **(A1)**; $\Delta H=-\dfrac{2.84}{0.0500}=-57\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ **(A1)** — negative because the reaction is exothermic.

prompt: Burning 0.46 g of ethanol (M = 46.08) heats 200 g of water by 11.5 °C. Calculate the enthalpy of combustion of ethanol and explain why it is much less exothermic than the data-booklet value of −1367 kJ mol⁻¹.
markscheme:
$q=200\times4.18\times11.5=9.61\times10^{3}$ J; $n=0.00998$ mol **(M1)(A1)**

$\Delta H=-963\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ **(A1)**

Heat is lost to the surroundings (air, can), and combustion may be incomplete **(R1)**
